subject: How to return nothing (exit prematurely) from a downloadHandler?

messages.author: a1bf76ab9a5a2d4b
messages.subject: How to return nothing (exit prematurely) from a downloadHandler?
parts: Suppose I have a downloadHandler, and inside of it, while generating the content to download, I run into some error so I want to stop the function from returning a file and I DON'T want to download anything.  Simply using `return()` doesn't work, nor does using `stop()` to error out. I might be missing something very obvious, but I'm drawing blanks here...

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: How to return nothing (exit prematurely) from a downloadHandler?
parts: stop() doesn't do what you want? We can't stop the browser from opening, if that's what you're thinking--it's that new browser that's causing downloadHandler to run.

messages.subject: Re: How to return nothing (exit prematurely) from a downloadHandler?
parts:
Yes, stop() does cancel the download and shows a message on the newly opened window, but I was hoping for a way to just convey the error message in the original app window. I suppose I could programatically close the new window and somehow pass a variable to the other session?

Related question - is there a way to trigger a download without having the user click on the download button?  The use case is this: The user changes a bunch of options, clicks on a button, then I want to process the data, and only if it's all valid and good to go then I want to download. But I don't want to have to have them click on another button just to do the downloading.
